Native primarily to the snowy boreal forests of the Russian Far East and parts of northeastern China, adult males can grow up to 10–12 feet in length and weigh over 600 pounds, while females are noticeably smaller. They are uniquely adapted to extreme cold, featuring a dense, pale orange coat with fewer and wider stripes, a thick layer of belly fat, and shaggy winter fur. As solitary apex predators, their diet consists mainly of wild boar, elk, and deer, and they can consume up to 60 pounds of meat in a single meal. 🐅 UPDATE | FATAL TIGER ATTACK The young man mauled to death after entering a tiger enclosure in England has been identified in news reports as William Chapman. Newly surfaced footage reportedly shows Chapman filming himself approaching the tiger, Altai, moments before the attack. Social media photos also show him posing with a Bible and crossbow. Police confirmed he visited the park alone. Despite speculation that he had a developmental disability, no diagnosis has been publicly confirmed. Authorities continue investigating why he entered the enclosure. #WilliamChapman #TigerAttack #YorkshireWildlifePark #TrueCrime #CookiesWorld

This haunting footage was captured moments before the fatal tiger mauling in Yorkshire. Footage has emerged appearing to show a man in his 20s approaching a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park shortly before he was killed inside the enclosure on Saturday, October 10. The man can be seen filming himself near five-year-old Siberian tiger Altai as horrified visitors shout ‘Oh my God’ from the viewing platform above. Onlookers reportedly tried to stop him climbing over the barrier and entering the enclosure. The park remains closed following the tragedy, while it has been confirmed that Altai will not be euthanised.
